stories.title: Nevada wildfire forces tens of thousands to evacuate as blaze threatens city of Reno
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of people faced another night away from home on Monday as a wind-driven wildfire threatened Reno, Nevada, blanketing the city in smoke and closing schools. About 24,000 people remained under evacuation orders, down from more than 40,000 at the peak, while tens of thousands more were on alert.

stories.title: French tourist dies in Death Valley after car gets stuck in mud
stories.summary: A French tourist has died in California's Death Valley after becoming stranded on the side of the road during 46.6C (116F) heat. Police found 68-year-old Pierre Michel Formosa recently following a brief search, with the National Park service saying he died while trying to seek help in the blistering heat when his car got stuck in mud. "This is a heartbreaking reminder of how quickly conditions here can turn dangerous," Death Valley National Park Superintendent Mike Reynolds said in a statement. Soaring temperatures across the United States have caused millions of people to sweat through record heatwaves, leading to dozens of heat-related deaths. Formosa was driving through Death Valley with his French travelling companion last Monday when their vehicle became stuck in mud on West Side Road. The pair sought help by walking across the salt flats, before severe heat prevented the 68-year-old from continuing after 1.3 miles, according to the Death Valley National Park. The travelling companion managed to hail down a nearby driver, before rangers and police found Formosa later that afternoon where he was pronounced dead. "Death Valley is an extraordinary place, but its heat, distances, and remoteness can be dangerous, regardless of experience," Reynolds said. "We're grateful to everyone who took part in the search, and our thoughts are with his loved ones." Coroners would determine the cause and manner of his death, the national park said. An extreme heat warning is currently in effect across Death Valley, which brands itself as the "hottest place on Earth", according to its official website, having recorded a global high of 57C (134F) in 1913. Forecasters at the National Weather Service expected Southern California would experience its "hottest week of summer so far", the bureau said in a recent statement.

stories.title: DP vows police reform over mishandling of missing-person case
stories.summary: Democratic Party floor leader Han Byung-do said Tuesday that the ruling party will draw up a comprehensive plan to reform the police organization and establish a trustworthy investigation system. Han made the remarks one day after a body believed to be that of missing woman Jang Mi-ran was found on the southern resort island of Jeju following a delayed search caused by a police officer's false closure of her missing-person case. The case drew particular attention as the police are set to assume greater investigative responsibilities in October, when prosecutors will lose their independent and supplementary investigative powers under sweeping prosecution reforms spearheaded by the ruling party. "The Democratic Party will fulfill its responsibilities to the very end in devising a comprehensive plan for the reform of the police organization and establish an investigation system that the public can trust," Han said at a party meeting at the National Assembly. "We'll coolly reveal the police's wrongdoing and hold those responsible strictly accountable," he said, urging police leadership to thoroughly uncover the full circumstances surrounding the false closure of Jang's case. Han stressed that a police force that fails to earn the public's trust has no reason to exist. He then vowed not to allow Jang's case to fuel public anxiety and distrust over the new criminal justice system. "As police authority is set to expand, the police must further strengthen their investigative capabilities, accountability, transparency and democratic oversight," he said.
